thread.title: Renewed Support Predicted For Hong Kong Shares

title: Renewed Support Predicted For Hong Kong Shares
text:
Renewed Support Predicted For Hong Kong Shares September 27, 2018, 09:15: The Hong Kong stock market has moved lower in two of three trading days since the end of the four-day winning streak in which it had advanced more than 1,000 points or 3.7 percent. The Hang Seng Index now rests just above the 27,715-point plateau although it's expected to bounce higher again on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is firm, with support expected from the oil and technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are tipped to follow suit.
The Hang Seng finished modestly lower on Thursday following losses from the casinos and financials, while the oil and insurance companies were mixed.
For the day, the index sank 101.20 points or 0.36 percent to finish at 27,715.67 after trading between 27,638.54 and 27,928.29.
Among the actives, Galaxy plummeted 4.46 percent, while WH Group plunged 2.31 percent, CITIC surged 1.61 percent, CSPC Pharmaceutical tumbled 1.52 percent, Tencent Holdings skidded 1.39 percent, AIA Group spiked 1.32 percent, Sands China dropped 1.12 percent, New World Development retreated 0.93 percent, CNOOC advanced 0.67 percent, China Petroleum and Chemical (Sinopec) declined 0.65 percent, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China shed 0.52 percent, China Mobile added 0.40 percent, Ping An Insurance lost 0.38 percent, BOC Hong Kong fell 0.27 percent, Hong Kong & China Gas eased 0.13 percent and China Life Insurance was unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is upbeat as stocks opened higher on Thursday. They faded slightly in the afternoon but still finished firmly in the green.
The Dow added 54.65 points or 0.21 percent to 26,439.93, while the NASDAQ gained 51.60 points or 0.65 percent to 8,041.97 and the S&P was up 8.03 points or 0.28 percent to 2,914.00.
A notable advance by shares of Apple (AAPL) contributed to the higher close on Wall Street after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the company's stock with an Overweight rating.
In economic news, the Commerce Department noted a bigger than expected jump in durable goods orders in August. The Commerce Department also said the pace of U.S. economic growth in the second quarter was unrevised at 4.2 percent from the previous estimate.
Also, the Labor Department noted a rebound in initial jobless claims in the week ended September 22. And the National Association of Realtors said pending home sales dropped much more than expected in August.
Crude oil prices moved higher on Thursday, amid concerns that sanctions on Iran from November may result in supply shortage in the market. Crude oil futures for November delivery ended up $0.55 or 0.8 percent at $72.12 a barrel. //www.rttnews.com/2938884/renewed-support-predicted-for-hong-kong-shares.aspx
